summary: Slash-command contract catalogue covering explicit routing, z-plan's single-gate prose plan-brief + known-work DAG (work-graph.json), z-execute's INTENT-mode acceptance-evaluator/divergence-halt scheduler and native model routing, z-brainstorm/z-sharpen pre-planning, Hermes-marker integration (handoff/fanout/needs_input), and docs maintenance through doc-updater rather than ad hoc index edits.

entry_points.summary: Propagates approved changes through plan artifacts; `--skip-user-gate` for programmatic callers (e.g. `/z-review-all` auto-amend); Phase 9 elevation proposer after finalize.

Source/dev-only middle-gear attended chain orchestrator; excluded from prod release artifacts and MCP tool lists. Default preset `attend-full` = `plan,audit,test,implement-all,review-all`. Auto-advances through chain; halts inline only on four categories (decision/risk/shortcut/archiving); yields for `/clear` at context boundaries.

Audits plan artifacts for code-quality issues; requires STYLE.md (hard gate); emits PLAN_STYLE_AUDIT.md; Phase 5 resolver pre-check; `check-no-ask` halt branch emitting `plan_style_halt`; Phase 9 elevation proposer.

Pre-implementation plan audit: reality-check, best-practices, adversarial cross-LLM review, Class-tagged synthesis, default-amend gate (Phase 5). Auto_split default: spec_gap findings batch into one `/z-amend` call; premise_failure rendered as amendment-brief prose. Phase 9 elevation proposer.

Read-only multi-dimension audits; Phase 0 scope probe (LIGHT/MEDIUM/HEAVY) with single-file fast-path (`scope_probe_skipped_fast_path`); `--scope-from` for HEAVY sub-flow fan-out; Phase 2a draws up to 4 distinct `audit_persona` personas (`personas.audit`, default ON); Phase 4a measured advisory consult arm (`personas.consult_eval`, default OFF). Active-plan registry lifecycle.

Source/dev-only axiom approval command; excluded from prod release artifacts and MCP tool lists. Approves a candidate after showing evidence/falsifiability state; requires explicit confirmation; regenerates KERNEL.md synchronously on approval.

Source/dev-only axiom edit command; excluded from prod release artifacts and MCP tool lists. Edits a field on a candidate or approved axiom record; re-validates graph and regenerates kernel on approved records.
Source/dev-only axiom listing command; excluded from prod release artifacts and MCP tool lists. Renders a read-only table filtered by `--status`, `--scope`, or `--discipline`.
Source/dev-only axiom rejection command; excluded from prod release artifacts and MCP tool lists. Rejects a candidate or approved axiom, moving it to the rejected/tombstone store.
Source/dev-only axiom mining command; excluded from prod release artifacts and MCP tool lists. Mines candidate axioms via `axiom-extractor`; proposes only, never auto-approves.

Cheap parallel ideation with conversational tail. Phase 0: shared z-sharpen component runs when `GRILL.md` is absent (wrapper not invoked; no auto-dispatch); NL count parse (WIDE_N, default 3; emits `count_parsed`); scope probe `per_vendor`/`per_framing` axis; wide×HEAVY suppression (D2). Phase 2a: 3 distinct `ideator` personas when `brainstorm.personas` ON. Phase 2c (WIDE_N>3): conversational cost gate; phased overflow waves (cap 3, anti-seed, distinct personas); `ideator-clusterer` (Haiku) collapses N framings→K directions. Phase 3: ranked prose briefing + HARD end-turn guardrail (MUST NOT auto-decide). Phase 4 LIGHT/MEDIUM: discussion loop (ask/combine/re-spin cap 3/lock-in/abandon; `synthesized` default chosen_framing). Phase 4 HEAVY: ranked-pair briefing + end-turn.
Read-only single-phase command. Analyzes context utilization via `scripts/context-budget.py` and surfaces actionable savings recommendations. Registers/deregisters in active-plan registry (advisory).
Read-only lazy-code debt ledger. Scans for `z:` debt markers, renders grouped ledger to stdout. No LLM analysis, no subagent dispatch. `--save` writes to `Z-DEBT.md`.

Heavy hypothesis-tournament debugging with post-mortem and Phase 10 memory review (shipped branch only); 10-strategy Phase 2 feedback-loop escalation ladder; bisect at Phase 2.5; `repro_confidence` field; Phase 10 sequential AskUser loop capped at 3 candidates; emits `memory_review_terminal`. Active-plan registry lifecycle. Phases 3a/3b/7 use fixed 5-panel when `experiment.persona_rotation=true`; Phases 3a/3b draw distinct `consultant` personas when `personas.critique_panel` ON; Phase 7 fix-consult emits `selection_source=fixed_panel` for all arms (no persona prefix draw by design).
**Deprecated compatibility wrapper.** Routes to `/z-plan --quick`; do not present it as the current tiny plan-free command. Keep only for historical/user muscle-memory references.
Tier 2 narrative doc command. Reads finalized `tier2-context.json` and produces ADRs, design rationale, tradeoff explanations, and migration guides. Memoized by hash of `tier2-context.json`.

Read-only single-phase command. Evaluates a completed z-harness session archive via `scripts/evaluate-session.py` for patterns worth preserving as memories or skills. Surfaces candidates to user with `/z-suggest-memory` recommendation.

One-shot structured code/system explanation at a chosen depth lens (orientation/walkthrough/deep/audit-brief). Supports `/z-explain --repo orientation` for one-answer repo orientation via bounded surface mapping; `--surface=off` preserves current grounding path. For installed prod packages, pair `/z-explain` with `/z-learn` for user-facing understanding; `/z-explore` is source/dev-only terrain discovery. File:line citations required. Handoff to `/z-learn` when interactive exploration warranted; route completed-work reporting to `/z-report`. Telemetry: `explain_run_start` / `explain_run_end`.
Source/dev-only active depth-scaled codebase terrain discovery; excluded from prod release artifacts and MCP tool lists. `/z-map` is legacy source/dev compatibility only.

Exports skill/agent/persona sources through runtime drivers. Public prod defaults center Claude, OMP, and Codex; non-core hosts remain explicit dev/advanced/export-only targets. Generated mirrors belong under scratch output such as `temp/exports/`, not release source.

Ships diagnosed bug fixes with consult and Codex review; slug-confirm resolver gate (`workflow.slug_confirm`) after hard collision check; `check-no-ask` halt branch emitting `fix_halt`. Advisory eval-reviewer (`personas.review_eval`, default ON).
verify→done transition via human approval (`--via=human`) or 11-point audit evidence validation (`--via=audit --evidence=<path>`). Nest-guarded.
Any-state → dismissed; requires `--reason`; terminal. Nest-guarded.
Read-only merged view of project+global sinks, priority-sorted; filters `--status=`, `--sink=`, `--priority=`; `--json` for machine consumers. Nest-guarded.
Interactive follow-up consumer: priority-sorted selection, worktree check, staleness check, claim under lock, execute recommended_command, status writeback, auto-close attempt. Nest-guarded.
Re-stamps staleness data for blocked entries; transitions them back to open. Only valid for staleness-blocked entries. Nest-guarded.
Diagnostic counts per status, lock state, oldest open entry, last Notion sync error. Read-only. Nest-guarded.

Installer for the git-safety PreToolUse hook (`scripts/block-dangerous-git.sh`). Subcommands: `install` (AskUser global vs project scope; idempotent additive merge into `settings.json`; verify dry-run), `remove`, `status`. RUNTIME-GATE before scope AskUser.

Depth-first requirements interview: one question at a time with a recommended answer; self-serves codebase questions via Explore (Haiku); standing stop offer after every answer. Stages to `<plans-base>/.grill-pending.md`; finalizes to `$Z_HARNESS_PLAN_DIR/<slug>/GRILL.md`. Handoff recommends `/z-plan` or `/z-brainstorm`. Telemetry: `grill_run_start` / `grill_question` / `grill_finalized` / `phase_end`.

Writes `handoff.json` (protocol-version 1.0/1.1, 7 fields: `protocol_version`, `timestamp`, `agent`, `slug`, `status`, `next_step`, `context_files`) for session continuity across `/clear` boundaries. Universal across pi, Claude Code, Codex CLI. Producer-side of the handoff-protocol schema. Phase 3b: when `HERMES_MARKER_FILE` is set, emits a `handoff_continue` marker via `emit-hermes-marker.sh --strict` (a genuine write failure surfaces and exits non-zero rather than stranding the session — this is what makes user-triggered `/z-handoff`, not just the automatic clear-checkpoint path, Hermes-consumable). Phase 5 always prints a fenced copy-paste resume block with the FULL untruncated `next_step` (not the old truncated 80-char summary line), shown whether or not Hermes is managing the session.
Writes watcher-readable `handoff.json`, preserves existing `SESSION.md`, and emits `clear_checkpoint_written` so Oh My Pi, Hermes, MCP, or future watchers can clear and resume.

Orchestrates task queue with fresh subagents, reviewers, auto memory review (Phase 9). Supports both `IMPLEMENT_MODE=legacy` (TASKS.md main loop) and `IMPLEMENT_MODE=intent` (known-work DAG scheduler over `work-graph.json`/`LEDGER.md` with a T024 acceptance-evaluator seam (`intent-schema.py evaluate-acceptance`) at every durable settle point, plus a `divergence_signal` halt that routes to `/z-amend --reopen-intent` when a settled frontier invalidates the frozen INTENT). Phase 0.0 active-plan registry lifecycle after structural validation; Phase 0.1 consumer check (emits `implement_halted_followup_running`). N=2 cross-cluster parallel dispatch requires BOTH `overlap_count==0` AND `workflow.hermes_enabled=true` (default false → serial); intra-level `workflow.intent_parallel_levels` parallelism is additionally gated on parseable per-sibling `**Files:**` scope, `workstreams.json scope_unknown:false`, disjoint file scope, and a fan-out cap of 3. Cycle-2 skip-on-clean-cycle-1; `check-no-ask` halt branch on second review failure emitting `task_halt`+`implement_end`. Implementer model resolved via native `[model_routing.implementer]`/`[model_classes]` routing (`runtime.dispatch.dispatcher.resolve_implementer_model`); emits `subagent_model_source/route/route_kind/override_applied/override_support` telemetry. REMOTE_VERIFY dispatch is per-task in legacy mode but coalesced to one `remote-runner` build per BFS level boundary in INTENT mode. Hermes-managed mode (`HERMES_MARKER_FILE` set): `resolve-question` gates emit a `needs_input` marker via `emit-hermes-marker.sh` instead of `AskUserQuestion`. Step 5.0 persona-rotation block: implementer draw; `personas.implementer_retry` knob. Canonical Advisory eval-reviewer shared snippet (`<!-- ADVISORY-EVAL-REVIEWER -->` anchor). Steps 6+7a consult-aware: `Z_HARNESS_CONSULT=off` → `self-reviewer` subagent, emitting `no_consult_dispatch`+`self_review_completed`; consult=on → dual reviewer (base codex + advisory random-arm when `personas.review_eval` ON). Phase 9: persists candidates to JSONL, emits `memory_review_complete`, no in-phase AskUser loop.
Retrospects one run and proposes harness improvements.

Bootstraps two-tier human and LLM documentation; also creates repo-root `CONTEXT.md` (domain glossary) by default — `--no-glossary` to skip. Idempotent: re-run extends without clobbering user terms. RUNTIME-GATE before Explore and AskUser.

Interactive progressive-disclosure tutor for code/system understanding. Four depth lenses; resumable `.learn-pending.md` staging; optional `LEARN.md` finalize. Standing navigation menu each turn. Ingests prior `/z-explain` context. Completed-work reports remain `/z-report`. Telemetry: `learn_run_start` / `learn_turn` / `learn_finalized`.

Refreshes stale concept docs (applies by default; `--dry-run` to preview), keeping human docs, LLM concept JSON, and INDEX metadata synchronized through doc-updater proposals. `--glossary` flag also refreshes repo-root `CONTEXT.md`. Stops for confirmation only on genuine-risk signals (memories_lost mismatch, or audit reject/needs-review under `--audit`).
Source/dev-only legacy compatibility wrapper. Delegates to `/z-explore --depth=deep`; excluded from prod release artifacts and MCP tool lists.
Reviews branch diffs into ranked task-shaped findings; requires STYLE.md.

Source/dev-only unattended pipeline orchestrator; excluded from prod release artifacts and MCP tool lists. Chains sub-commands via `Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt`; writes MORNING_REPORT.md on completion/halt.

Read-only persona registry inspector. Subcommands: `list`, `roles` (default), `validate`, `read <name>`, `where <name>`. Shows effective role bindings, enumerates persona files, validates registry, reads body, or locates a persona file. Never writes any file.

Splits large work into one-level cluster plans. Active-plan registry lifecycle: registers in Setup, seeds scope, runs overlap scan, deregisters on completion or abort (FINALIZE_STATUS rule). Uses `all_plan_slugs` for collision detection. When Hermes fanout is requested (or a `handoff_fanout` marker will be emitted), Phase 5 ensures `workstreams.json` exists (`scripts/generate-workstreams.py`) and emits a fanout payload (`slug`, `group_id`, `workstreams_path`, `handoff_paths`, `shared_concerns_path`, `ack_required`, `partial_tree`) that Hermes consumes via MCP `so_start_fanout` to start one grouped child session per ready workstream.

Default path is a conversational intent compiler: sharpen first (`GRILL.md`), ask before optional `/z-brainstorm`, draft and iterate `INTENT.md`, flag concerns/decisions plus optional audit-plan scan, then a single unified final-approval gate. `--full` remains the legacy SPEC.md + PLAN.md + TASKS.md compatibility path. Route checks and brainstorm/audit recommendations ask rather than auto-dispatch. Watcher-managed checkpoint seams use `check-compaction.sh` / `write-clear-checkpoint.sh` before high-context planning and before `/z-execute`. Final approval (Phase 5) renders one dense prose plan brief (intent, approach, high-impact decisions with tradeoffs, shortcuts, inlined `intent-readthrough-flags.md`, acceptance criteria) and asks ONE gate — approve / reject-shortcuts / amend / grill the draft / return to sharpen-brainstorm / stop — replacing the old per-decision and per-shortcut `AskUserQuestion` popups; a shortcut is approved only when the brief containing it is approved. "Grill the draft" runs an inline post-draft grill loop seeded from `intent-readthrough-flags.md` (emits `post_draft_grill`, writes `post-draft-grill.md`) before re-rendering the brief. On approval, generates `TASKS.md`, an initial append-only `work-graph.json` known-work DAG (nodes derived from TASKS.md `**Files:**`/`**Depends on:**`/`**Advances:**`, `level_hint` = dependency depth) for `/z-execute`'s INTENT-mode scheduler, task-to-intent mapping, workstreams/execution strategy, `HANDOFF.md`, and watcher-readable checkpoint metadata.
Probes PATH for LLM CLIs and writes `providers.json` with role bindings. Enforces `consultant_primary != consultant_secondary`. Atomic write via tmpfile+rename.

Profile-aware, read-only narrative for completed work: evidence, backtests, feature writeups, technical handoffs, and external/shareable updates. Produces one report at one tier/profile; writes `REPORT.md` for run/slug targets or `--save` output when requested.

Read-only work-thread recovery for fuzzy or exact prior-work targets. Selects a bounded plan/run/worktree/branch/artifact/repo context, reports ambiguity explicitly, and recommends safe continuation commands without executing them. `--report` reuses `/z-report` only after target selection; noninteractive ambiguity returns `needs_selection`.
Source/dev-only heavy meta-orchestrator; excluded from prod release artifacts and MCP tool lists. Composes `/z-explore --depth=deep` and `/z-brainstorm`, then adversarial synthesis panel.

Final-gate cross-LLM review of cumulative diff vs plan contract. Phase 0 consumer check (emits `review_halted_followup_running`). Phase 3.7.5 routes non-halting findings to project sink (`followups_routed_to_sink`). Phase 6.5 unconditionally auto-amends every spec_gap via `/z-amend --skip-user-gate`; writes `auto-amend-log.md`; emits `auto_amend_applied`. Phase 6.6 renders unified amendment brief via `scripts/amendment-brief.py`; skipped when both lists empty. `check-no-ask` halt branch (`review_halt`) with `.review_state.json` resume at Phase 3.7. Phase 7: auto memory review, `memory_review_complete`, no in-phase AskUser loop.

Configuration cockpit: inspect resolved state (default), run guided concern-grouped wizard (`wizard [--scope <name>]`), or apply a posture preset (`apply --posture <name>`). Delegates to `scripts/setup.py`. Seven wizard scopes: notifications, workflow, overnight, providers, personas, docs, memories.

Reusable bounded sharpening component plus slash-command wrapper. The component assesses clarity/alternatives, returns `proceed`, `sharpen_more`, or `route_to_brainstorm`, and can produce `GRILL.md`; callers such as `/z-brainstorm` reuse only that component. The wrapper owns empty-topic bootstrap, slug/collision handling, telemetry, final GRILL.md write, and advisory handoff. Neither surface auto-dispatches `/z-plan` or `/z-brainstorm`.
Diagnoses and patches misleading skill or command files.

Reports read-only run progress, timing, cost, next step, and recent memory-review activity (Phase 4b). Phase 0b prints resolved base, repo-id, and active-plan count from the registry unconditionally (not gated behind any env var).

Authors STYLE.md from idiomatic source captures and cross-LLM critique; `--amend` mines dismissal clusters. Mode A refuses if STYLE.md exists; Mode B refuses if STYLE.md absent. Phase 4 parallel critique; `--ingest` skips interview and Capture phases.

**Known-broken procedure body.** The `--source` prefix table and `--kind routing-preference` structured-write mode (target `docs/llm/workflow.json` / `docs/llm/workflow-<project-slug>.json`) are documented and intact, but the general interactive memory-authoring body was lost in the commands/→skills/ migration: line ~60 reads "Read and execute `skills/z-suggest-memory/SKILL.md` in full" — a self-reference to its own file, not a working delegation target. Do not describe general (non-`--kind routing-preference`, non-`--from-candidate-json`) invocation as a working procedure until this is fixed.
Drafts semantic TESTS.md cases and links them to tasks.

Thin host wrapper: runs the deterministic `z-harness update` / `python3 -m z_harness_cli update` CLI and surfaces its exact result verbatim. The skill body performs no manifest fetch, no schema validation, no tarball extraction, and no install-mode detection itself — the CLI (`z_harness_cli/commands/update.py`, `z_harness_cli/release.py`) owns all release-manifest and install-mode logic (wheel/uv upgrade, clean-checkout `git pull --ff-only`, or manifest-backed reinstall guidance for tarball/runtime installs).

Tiered bulk codebase quality uplift: decompose, cross-cut, per-component audits, sequential implement. Slug-confirm resolver gate (`workflow.slug_confirm`) after hard collision check; `check-no-ask` halt branch emitting `uplift_halt`. MANIFEST.md single source of truth; resumable via `--retry-bailed`, `--refresh-component`.

Interactive understanding command. Reconstructs what a codebase feature actually does, cross-references against what was intended, and converges on a verified model. Delegates to `skills/z-verify/SKILL.md`. Supports `--slug`, `--path`, `--concept` targeting.

Read-only concurrent-run diagnostic. No LLM calls, no subagent dispatch, no writes. Phase 0 prints resolved base + repo-id. Phase 1 lists all active plans from registry table (slug, command, phase, branch, current_task, age, status). Phase 2 optionally shows path-overlap with a specific run-id (`--run-id <id>` or `Z_HARNESS_RUN_ID`). Robust to registry unavailability.

invariants: Commands are Markdown procedure specs; planning, research, audit, and test commands do not write production code unless explicitly scoped to do so.
Route checks collect deterministic signals first; planning-router is advisory only when deterministic signals conflict.
Every route decision writes route-decision.md, emits plan_route_decision, asks the user, and never auto-executes the target command.
Primary routes are z-do, z-plan, z-plan-split, z-brainstorm, and z-sharpen; contextual exits include z-audit-plan, z-fix, z-debug, z-amend, and z-maintain-docs.
z-audit-plan is valid only with existing plan artifacts and remains read-only.
Review-family commands preserve evidence separately and promote only actionable findings into task-shaped artifacts consumed by z-execute --tasks.
z-execute preserves fresh-context implementation by delegating tasks to implementer and reviewer subagents.

[registry] Run-creating commands (z-plan, z-execute, z-do, z-debug, z-audit, z-plan-split) register with active-plan-registry.py immediately after slug discovery and structural validation. Overlap is advisory (lockless safe); strict mode (Z_HARNESS_STRICT_OVERLAP=1) adds one hard gate on explicit x explicit exact path collision.

[registry] FINALIZE_STATUS rule: after REG_RC==0, any run-ending halt sets FINALIZE_STATUS=aborted and calls deregister --status aborted before exiting. Normal completion deregisters with complete. If register failed (REG_RC==3 or nonzero), never call deregister.

[registry] REG_RC==3 means register FAILED (no record written). Orchestrator logs registry_error, then: interactive -> AskUserQuestion proceed/abort; unattended -> proceed+log (or halt if Z_HARNESS_STRICT_OVERLAP=1). Any other nonzero REG_RC treated identically to REG_RC==3.

[registry] OVL_RC==0 proceed silently. OVL_RC==10 (advisory) AskUserQuestion: proceed/wait/abort; under Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK proceed+log. OVL_RC==20 (blocking) hard halt. Any other nonzero log registry_error and proceed.
[registry] z-where is purely read-only: no events, no writes, no LLM calls. Always exits cleanly even when registry unavailable.
[registry] z-stats Phase 0b reads active-plan count unconditionally (NOT gated behind any env var). Fallback: print 'Active plans: (registry unavailable)' and continue.

[rotation] When experiment.persona_rotation=true, z-execute draws one implementer persona per attempt via random-for-role (or forced-control on cadence); dual reviewer (base_codex + random_arm advisory when personas.review_eval=true); ONE persona_attempt_outcome per attempt at close.

[rotation] personas.implementer_retry knob (default 'same'): 'same' reuses cycle-1 persona-draw.json anchor across all cycles; 'new' draws fresh persona to persona-draw-v<CYCLE>.json sidecar; cycle-1 anchor NEVER overwritten on retry.
[rotation] When experiment.persona_rotation=false, all rotation behavior is a complete no-op.
[rotation] z-plan and z-debug use fixed 5-panel (selection_source=fixed_panel) when experiment.persona_rotation=true; no random draw for consultant phases unless personas.critique_panel=true.
[rotation] z-plan Phases 3 and 7 draw independent persona sets (random-distinct-for-role consultant --count=5). Phase 3 draw MUST NOT be reused for Phase 7.

[rotation] z-debug Phases 3a and 3b share the same consultant persona draw (drawn once before Phase 3a, reused at 3b). Phase 7 fix-consult uses fixed_panel for all arms — no persona prefix draw by design.
[rotation] z-brainstorm Phase 2a draws 3 distinct ideator personas when brainstorm.personas=true (default ON). Knob OFF is a complete no-op.
[rotation] z-audit Phase 2a draws up to 4 distinct audit_persona personas (personas.audit, default ON). Underflow is graceful: shorter array returned, unfilled slots run vanilla.
[rotation] personas.consult_eval (advisory consult arm, default OFF) applies to z-audit Phase 4a. Advisory arm output NEVER merged into neutral synthesis.

[rotation] personas.review_eval (advisory eval-reviewer, default ON) applies to z-fix, z-do, and z-execute. Advisory reviewer verdict NEVER changes pass/fail outcome, NEVER triggers retry. Canonical implementation is the shared snippet in skills/z-execute/SKILL.md (<!-- ADVISORY-EVAL-REVIEWER --> anchor).
[rotation] persona_attempt_outcome status field uses 'done' (not 'ok').
[rotation] Random-arm reviewer verdict is advisory only — MUST NOT change halt/retry behavior. Only base_codex reviewer determines review outcome.
Long consult-heavy phases use explicit compaction breakpoints or resumable state files where specified.
z-execute Phase 9 and z-review-all Phase 7 are soft auto-memory-review phases: all failure paths exit silently without halting. Phase 9 emits memory_review_complete (no in-phase AskUser loop).
z-debug Phase 10 is a soft auto-memory-review phase that DOES have a sequential AskUser loop (capped at 3 candidates) and emits memory_review_terminal. Abandoned branch skips entirely.
z-uplift never writes production code directly; orchestrates audits via auditor subagents and delegates implementation to z-execute.
z-uplift gates on STYLE.md presence and doc-staleness before decomposition; it never auto-invokes z-style-init or z-maintain-docs.
z-uplift MANIFEST.md is the single source of truth for component state across phases and resumes; all state transitions are atomic via tmp-then-rename writes.
The cross-cutting synthetic component is excluded from Phase 3 per-component audit iteration and handled in Phase 5 only.
perf is excluded from z-uplift default dimensions to bound cost; must be added explicitly via --dimensions.
z-style-init Mode A refuses if STYLE.md already exists; Mode B refuses if STYLE.md does not exist.
z-export delegates all file I/O to adapter scripts; the command itself performs no writes.
z-providers-discover enforces consultant_primary != consultant_secondary before writing providers.json.
z-providers-discover writes atomically via tmpfile+rename.
z-audit-plan-style requires STYLE.md at repo root; there is no --no-style escape.
z-audit-plan-style is read-only; plan mutations happen only via /z-amend applied to surviving PLAN_STYLE_AUDIT.md findings.
z-audit Phase 0 (scope-probe) is skipped when --scope-from is present; SKIP_PHASE_0=true is set before slug derivation, doc-fetcher, or run_start logging.

z-audit Phase 0 also has a single-file fast-path: when the target is a single file path with no whitespace, scope-probe is skipped and the target is auto-classified as LIGHT; emits scope_probe_skipped_fast_path.
z-brainstorm Phase 0 also has a single-file fast-path identical in structure to z-audit's; emits scope_probe_skipped_fast_path with command=z-brainstorm.
z-brainstorm Phase 0 uses axis taxonomy [per_vendor, per_framing]; low-confidence probe results downgrade to MEDIUM without AskUser in v1a.
z-brainstorm HEAVY Phase 4 presents a (chunk x framing) selection matrix via end-turn prose briefing, never a popup.
z-brainstorm HEAVY abandons set chosen_framing: abandoned (not chosen_pair) to keep abandon detection uniform across LIGHT/MEDIUM/HEAVY modes.
All commands that fire notifications call scripts/config.py should-notify --event <type> and act only when the return is yes.
Commands that send notifications or apply docs call scripts/config.py export-env during Setup before any phase runs.
Resolver hooks (resolve-question) branch on {result: skip|prefill|ask}; a resolver error always falls back to asking the user normally.
The hard slug-collision check (PLAN.md/TASKS.md already in slug dir) runs unconditionally in z-plan, z-fix, and z-uplift before resolve-question is called.
z-audit-plan Phase 9, z-audit-plan-style Phase 9, and z-amend Phase 9 are soft elevation-proposer phases: if propose-prefs.py returns empty or nonzero exit, the phase is skipped silently.

z-suggest-memory --kind routing-preference writes to docs/llm/workflow.json (global) or docs/llm/workflow-<project-slug>.json (project); file created with INDEX.json registration if absent; MEMORIES-FLAT.md regenerated after every write.
z-plan step 9c is the sole consolidated freshness gate covering docs-staleness, research-staleness, and map-staleness in one AskUserQuestion.

z-research Phase 1 dispatches /z-map and /z-brainstorm in a single parallel message when both need to run. Sub-run identification uses the first event's kind field (map_run_start vs brainstorm_run_start) in events.jsonl.

z-execute N=2 cross-cluster parallel dispatch fires only when overlap_count==0 in SHARED-CONCERNS.md frontmatter AND workflow.hermes_enabled=true (default false -> always serial; this is Hermes-specific machinery, not a general optimization).
z-execute cycle-2 skip-on-clean-cycle-1 fires when CYCLE==2 AND cycle-1 reviewer returned blockers=0 AND majors=0, regardless of why the implementer re-ran.
check-no-ask is fail-closed: it returns halt|proceed and correctly handles Z_HARNESS_ASK_ALL=1 vs Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt conflicts (exit 5). Exit 5 is a hard config-conflict error.

Seven commands are instrumented with check-no-ask halt branches: z-plan (plan_halt x2), z-fix (fix_halt), z-uplift (uplift_halt), z-audit-plan (audit_halt), z-audit-plan-style (plan_style_halt), z-review-all (review_halt + .review_state.json), z-execute (task_halt + implement_end on second review failure).
z-overnight sets Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt ONLY around each Skill call; the parent orchestrator's own AskUserQuestion prompts run with NO_ASK unset.
z-review-all halted-state resume: if .review_state.json has halted: true AND halt_reason: no_ask_blocked, emit review_resume_from_halt and jump to Phase 3.7 re-run.

Phase 0 consumer check in z-execute and z-review-all reads index.view.json as a dict with entries as an object (not a list); uses entries_obj.values(). A missing or malformed index.view.json yields RUNNING_COUNT=0.
All six z-followup-* commands carry a nest guard (Z_HARNESS_FOLLOWUP_CALLER_DEPTH >= 1) that fires before any other logic.
z-followup-next is the only followup command that acquires per-entry locks; it checks the global cross-tool lock before claiming.

z-attend Invariant 1: any gate with no explicit halt category resolves to 'ask', never 'mechanical_proceed'. Gate policy lives in z-attend.md; sequencing mechanics live in chain-runner.sh (Invariant 2).
z-axiom-scan proposes only — never auto-approves. z-axiom-approve requires explicit user confirmation before any kernel regeneration.
z-personas is read-only — it never writes any file.
z-context-budget and z-evaluate are read-only single-phase commands; they perform no subagent dispatch and no code edits.
z-debt is read-only unless --save flag is explicitly passed; no LLM analysis, no auto-upgrade, no subagent dispatch.
z-setup delegates configuration state reads/writes to scripts/setup.py; the command itself does not directly mutate TOML.

z-review-all Phase 6.5 unconditionally auto-amends every amendment_proposal (spec_gap) via /z-amend --skip-user-gate; no per-finding popup; writes auto-amend-log.md; emits auto_amend_applied per amendment. Phase 6.6 renders unified amendment brief via amendment-brief.py when either list is non-empty.

z-audit-plan Phase 5 default (source==none) is auto_split: INTENT-mode batches all spec_gap into ONE /z-amend call; legacy-mode per-finding; premise_failure rendered via amendment-brief.py as conversational prose. force_ask fires only when amend-gate-decision.py returns force_ask.

Z_HARNESS_CONSULT=off is detected via resolve-provider.py returning the none sentinel — NOT by reading the env var directly. Commands that check for none: z-plan (consultant_primary, Phases 3+7), z-execute (reviewer, Steps 6+7a).

consult_skipped (z-plan) and no_consult_dispatch (z-execute) are distinct event kinds. consult_skipped carries {phase:3} or {phase:7}; no_consult_dispatch carries {id, reason, reviewer_replaced_by: self_review} per task-cycle.
z-plan is a workflow.pre_run_cost_gate hard callsite before planning-router, intent-classifier, doc-fetcher, Explore, consultant panels, task-tree-generator, or any other expensive Agent dispatch.
z-plan nonterminal cost-reduction attempts emit cost_gate_reestimate_attempt; exactly one terminal cost_gate_decision is emitted per run.
z-plan terminal cost-gate halt/abandon/interrupted paths finalize and render Run Brief before claim release and deregister.
Planning route checks and final handoff gates surface user choices and never auto-dispatch the recommended command.
/z-plan records explicit Intent-vs-Full SDD mode before hard cost gating; config/flags only preselect unless unattended/no-ask binds the recommendation.
/z-brainstorm uses the shared z-sharpen component when GRILL.md is absent; it does not invoke the /z-sharpen wrapper.
/z-maintain-docs plus doc-updater is the intended path for concept docs and INDEX updates; no ad hoc index-only surgery.

z-execute supports IMPLEMENT_MODE=intent (known-work DAG scheduler over work-graph.json/LEDGER.md, T024 acceptance-evaluator seam at every durable settle point via intent-schema.py evaluate-acceptance) alongside legacy IMPLEMENT_MODE=legacy (TASKS.md main loop); mode is detected once via the SPEC.md-presence seam and the legacy path below that seam is CLOSED for modification.

z-execute INTENT-mode acceptance evaluator treats unknown as unmet (conservative continue) except for a narrow, evidence-backed prose/doc-plan exception: the orchestrator may terminate only with documented per-criterion line-level evidence when the diff is predominantly doc/markdown and criteria read as prose assertions; a criterion with no concrete file evidence still stays unmet.

z-execute INTENT-mode divergence halt: after VERDICT: continue, the orchestrator scans the just-settled LEDGER.md level section for a divergence_signal line; if present it emits intent_bfs_divergence, sets FINALIZE_STATUS=aborted, deregisters, and recommends /z-amend --reopen-intent <slug> instead of continuing the DAG scheduler.

z-execute REMOTE_VERIFY dispatch is per-task (remote-runner Haiku subagent) in legacy mode, but coalesced to exactly one remote-runner build per BFS level boundary (union of the settled frontier's REMOTE_VERIFY commands) when LEVEL_EXECUTE_ACTIVE=1 in INTENT mode; a coalesced-build failure halts the whole level, not a single task.

z-execute implementer model selection resolves through native [model_routing.implementer] + [model_classes] config (runtime.dispatch.dispatcher.resolve_implementer_model), tiered low|medium->sonnet, high|retry->opus by default; the resolution records override_applied/override_support because native per-call model override is host-dependent and may be advisory-only telemetry rather than an applied override.

z-execute safe intent parallelism (workflow.intent_parallel_levels=true) is gated by additional safety checks beyond the knob: every sibling task in the level must have a parseable precise **Files:** scope, workstreams.json (when present) must report scope_unknown:false, eligible siblings must have disjoint file scope with no workstream dependency/conflict edge, and the batch is capped/partitioned to INTENT_PARALLEL_FANOUT_LIMIT=3. Missing/unparseable scope or scope_unknown:true serializes the whole affected level (not discretionary).

Hermes-managed sessions are detected via the HERMES_MARKER_FILE env var: when set, resolve-question gates emit a needs_input marker (via emit-hermes-marker.sh) instead of AskUserQuestion, and z-execute/z-handoff emit status/heartbeat/done/handoff_continue markers best-effort (except z-handoff Phase 3b's handoff_continue emit, which uses emit-hermes-marker.sh --strict and exits non-zero on genuine write failure).

z-handoff Phase 3b is the one --strict emit-hermes-marker.sh callsite in the codebase; all other emit-hermes-marker.sh callers (including write-clear-checkpoint.sh) remain best-effort by design (a fatal emit mid-/z-execute checkpoint would abort the checkpoint contract).

z-plan Phase 5 final approval is a SINGLE prose plan-brief gate (intent, approach, high-impact decisions with tradeoffs, shortcuts, inlined intent-readthrough-flags.md, acceptance criteria) with six branches (approve / reject-shortcuts / amend / grill the draft / return to sharpen-brainstorm / stop) -- it replaced the earlier per-decision AskUserQuestion + per-shortcut AskUserQuestion popup sequence. A shortcut is approved only when the brief containing it is approved as written.

z-plan's post-draft grill loop (reachable only from the Phase 5 single gate's "grill the draft" branch) is an inline /z-grill-style interrogation seeded from intent-readthrough-flags.md, not an automatic handoff to the /z-grill command; it emits post_draft_grill and writes post-draft-grill.md before re-rendering the brief.

z-plan writes an initial append-only work-graph.json known-work DAG after final approval (nodes derived from TASKS.md **Files:**/**Depends on:**/**Advances:**, level_hint = dependency depth via depends_on); this is a frontier, not a claimed-complete task tree -- z-execute's INTENT-mode scheduler appends newly discovered nodes as implementation outcomes make additional work knowable.

z-plan-split supports Hermes multi-session fanout: when fanout is requested, Phase 5 ensures workstreams.json exists (scripts/generate-workstreams.py) and emits a fanout payload (slug, group_id, workstreams_path, handoff_paths, shared_concerns_path, ack_required, partial_tree) that Hermes consumes via MCP so_start_fanout to start one grouped child session per ready workstream (skipping failed workstreams by default).

The canonical prod-visibility manifest implementation is runtime.release_surface as of the codex-prod-support/model-routing work; z_harness_cli.release_surface is now a thin re-export shim over it, not the canonical source. Codex is a core public export/release target alongside Claude and OMP (promoted from a non-core/advanced target).

z-suggest-memory's --kind routing-preference structured-write mode and --source prefix conventions are intact and working; the general interactive/--from-candidate-json memory-authoring procedure body is a known-broken self-referential stub (the file instructs reading and executing itself) left over from the commands/->skills/ migration -- do not present general invocation as a working procedure.

Percentage-based adaptive context compaction (scripts/check-compaction.sh / scripts/write-clear-checkpoint.sh, percentage-threshold-evaluated seams rather than fixed points) is wired as a shared cross-command mechanism through z-plan, z-execute, z-audit, z-debug, z-review-all, z-test, z-uplift, z-research, z-explore, z-handoff, z-clear-checkpoint, and z-map (via its z-explore delegation).
gotchas: [registry] z-plan Phase 0.0 ordering: register runs AFTER slug discovery, collision check, and resolver gate. Pre-validation register creates a zombie record with no deregister path.
[registry] z-execute Phase 0.0 ordering: registration must occur AFTER Setup steps 1, 2, 2b, and 3. All tree-validation abort paths before Phase 0.0 have no record to deregister.
[registry] scope-extractor subagent: update-scope returns 0 by design and self-logs registry_error on internal failure. Do NOT add redundant || log after the call.
[rotation] persona_attempt_outcome is emitted by the orchestrator at attempt close, not by the implementer subagent.
[rotation] personas.implementer_retry='same' (default): REUSE=1 set from cycle-1 anchor persona-draw.json. The cycle-1 anchor NEVER overwritten on retry.
[rotation] On retry, implementer_retry='new' uses --exclude so retry gets a different persona. Prior persona not guaranteed to be excluded when pool is large.
[rotation] z-debug Phase 7 fix-consult emits selection_source=fixed_panel for all arms even when experiment.persona_rotation=true — no persona prefix draw for Phase 7. Do not reuse the Phase 3a draw.
[rotation] z-plan Phases 3 and 7 draws are independent: each phase calls random-distinct-for-role consultant --count=5 separately. Phase 3 draw MUST NOT be forwarded to Phase 7.
[rotation] personas.consult_eval default is false (OFF). Unlike personas.review_eval (ON by default), must be explicitly enabled.
[rotation] personas.review_eval advisory arm fires ONLY when BOTH experiment.persona_rotation AND personas.review_eval are both true.
Do not add z-audit-plan as a front-door planning route when no plan exists; route to z-plan instead.
z-execute --tasks derives BASE from the provided tasks file and bypasses normal slug/tree discovery.
z-suggest-memory is a thin delegator; memory mutation lives in commands/z-suggest-memory.md.
Plain z-maintain-docs applies refreshed docs by default; pass --dry-run to preview without writing.
--from-candidate-json on z-suggest-memory accepts a file path or - (stdin); it is the automated path used by Phase 9/Phase 7/Phase 10 only.

z-execute Phase 9 does NOT present a sequential AskUserQuestion loop — it persists all candidates to JSONL and push-notifies the user. The 3-candidate per-run cap applies only to z-debug Phase 10's in-phase AskUser loop.
z-debug Phase 10 memory review is skipped entirely on the abandoned branch; no memory_review_terminal event is emitted.
z-debug Phase 10 clears .notify-dedup-session at the start of each fresh invocation.
z-debug Phase 2.5 bisect fast-path: all three gates must hold. Non-ok bisect returns fall through to Phase 3a silently.
z-uplift slug collision detection presents one AskUserQuestion per colliding slug before COMPONENTS.md is written.
z-uplift --refresh-component archives both REPORT.md and TASKS.md atomically before resetting the MANIFEST row; both files must exist or the command exits with an error.
z-uplift resume detection reads MANIFEST state before entering any phase; SKIP_TO_PHASE guards must be checked at the top of every skippable phase.
z-style-init --amend Mode B exits early when DISMISSED_SIGNATURES is empty or N_CLUSTERS is 0 after Jaccard clustering with min-2-member filter.
z-style-init Phase 4 parallel critique: if both consultants fail, critique is skipped with a log event and the draft proceeds to user review unmodified.
z-providers-discover last-assignment-wins for multi-CLI role selections; consultant_primary/consultant_secondary collision triggers a reprompt loop.
z-export --target=all runs cursor, codex, agy sequentially — not in parallel. A failed target does not abort subsequent targets.
z-audit-plan-style archives any existing PLAN_STYLE_AUDIT.md before overwriting; this archive is what extract-dismissals.py reads for prior dismissal signatures.
z-audit --scope-from must be parsed BEFORE Setup (before slug derivation, doc-fetcher, or run_start logging).
z-brainstorm HEAVY Phase 4 Back-loop is capped at 3 iterations; the fourth Back is treated as Abandon.
z-brainstorm scope-probe low-confidence results are silently downgraded to MEDIUM in v1a — no AskUser gate.
Notification policy is now driven by config.py should-notify; do not check Z_HARNESS_NOTIFY_LEVEL directly.
The hard slug-collision check runs unconditionally before resolve-question in z-plan, z-fix, and z-uplift; a resolver result of 'skip' does NOT bypass the collision check.
z-plan step 9c to_command: null means the user chose to proceed with stale inputs or abandon — not a routing failure. /z-stats must not interpret null as an error.
z-execute cycle-2 skip-on-clean-cycle-1 fires regardless of why the implementer re-ran.
check-no-ask exit 5 means Z_HARNESS_ASK_ALL=1 and Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt are both set — hard config conflict, not a normal halt.
z-overnight v1 known limit: only 12 AskUserQuestion callsites are instrumented for halt-from-ask. Run scripts/lint-askuser.sh --strict before launching a long overnight chain.

Phase 0 consumer check parses index.view.json as a dict (entries is an object keyed by entry-id, not a list). A list-style parse silently reports 0 running entries — the T100 fix uses entries_obj.values().
z-followup-confirm --via=audit requires --evidence=<path>; --via=human is mutually exclusive with --evidence. Mixing is a hard argument-parse error.
z-followup-refresh only accepts entries in blocked state; other block reasons are rejected with an explicit error.
Z_HARNESS_CONSULT=off is detected via resolve-provider.py returning the none sentinel — NOT by reading the env var directly.
The self-reviewer subagent has no Edit or Write tools by design. Always use subagent_type='self-reviewer'.
z-attend gate policy separation Invariant 2: sequencing/state mechanics live in chain-runner.sh; z-attend owns only the gate category posture. Never hardcode the step list in z-attend.
z-axiom-scan never auto-approves; the user must explicitly call z-axiom-approve. z-axiom-approve regenerates the kernel synchronously on approval — this is synchronous and may take a moment.
z-verify delegates fully to skills/z-verify/SKILL.md; the command file itself is a one-line dispatch.
z-context-budget and z-evaluate both register/deregister in the active-plan registry even though they are read-only — this is advisory-only registration for visibility.

z-review-all Phase 6.5 auto-amends ALL spec_gap findings unconditionally (blocker/major/minor); only implementation_drift is left as candidate fixup tasks. Phase 6.6 is skipped when both corrections and approach_concerns lists are empty.

z-audit-plan auto_split path (source==none): INTENT-mode batches ALL spec_gap into a single /z-amend re-freeze, not per-finding. workflow.audit_to_amend is SOURCE-KEYED: stored value alone does not determine behavior; resolver source is the discriminator.

z-plan cost-reduction can only lower documented intent-depth/Phase-3 drivers and must re-run the hard gate; it does not mutate config or silently reduce doc_fetcher/explore/Phase-7/task-tree-generator dispatch.
A /z-sharpen or /z-brainstorm recommendation from planning-router or Phase 8.4 is a route gate result, not a command launch.
HANDOFF.md is written after TASKS in /z-plan and supports fresh-session audit/execute handoff; it is not the primary contract.
Do not patch docs/llm/INDEX.json by itself; update concept docs through /z-maintain-docs so human, LLM, and index tiers remain consistent.

z-suggest-memory: do not trust the file's own instruction at line ~60 ("read and execute skills/z-suggest-memory/SKILL.md in full") as a working delegation -- it is a self-reference stub; only --kind routing-preference and --from-candidate-json (automated review-agent path, schema documented) are verified working.

z-execute cross-cluster N=2 dispatch: overlap_count==0 alone is NOT sufficient -- workflow.hermes_enabled must also be true (default false). A plan with zero file overlap still runs clusters serially unless Hermes fanout is enabled.

z-execute divergence_signal is written by implementers/reviewers as a LEDGER_DECISIONS: entry, not a special API call; the orchestrator only scans LEDGER.md's ## Level N section text for the line after VERDICT: continue -- it is never checked on VERDICT: done.

z-execute REMOTE_VERIFY coalescing intentionally drops per-task cargo-check early feedback under LEVEL_EXECUTE_ACTIVE=1 -- this is the documented full-coalesce tradeoff (simplest failure-attribution story), not an oversight.

z-execute model routing: Z_HARNESS_RETRY_UPGRADE=opus or CYCLE>=2 selects the retry tier before **Complexity:** high is checked -- retry-on-cycle always wins over a first-attempt high-complexity opt-in.

z-plan Phase 5: 'reject shortcut(s)' and 'amend the brief' and 'grill the draft' all loop back to re-rendering the SAME single gate -- there is no separate approval step per revision; only 'approve as written' and 'stop' are terminal for this gate.

z-plan work-graph.json level_hint is computed via depends_on depth (0 for no deps), NOT the same value as z-execute's runtime CURRENT_LEVEL BFS counter -- level_hint is a static planning-time hint, not the live scheduler cursor.

z-handoff Phase 3b's --strict flag on emit-hermes-marker.sh only affects behavior when HERMES_MARKER_FILE is set; unset HERMES_MARKER_FILE is always a no-op regardless of --strict, so this block is invisible to pi/Claude Code/Codex CLI runs.

z-update's frontmatter/body no longer documents symlink-vs-tarball detection logic directly -- that entirely moved into z_harness_cli/commands/update.py and z_harness_cli/release.py; treat the skill file as a thin CLI-delegation wrapper, not a source of install-mode detection detail.

z-plan-split's Hermes fanout block only fires when fanout is requested or a handoff_fanout marker will be emitted; ordinary (non-Hermes) z-plan-split runs never touch workstreams.json generation from this path.

The human doc's entry-points table and this JSON's entry_points currently omit z-reconcile and z-test-prune, both real skills present in skills/ -- they were outside this refresh's given source_files scope; flag for a follow-up doc-updater pass rather than treating their absence as confirmed non-existence.
